comments.why_zh: 一场关于有生命土壤的长篇讲座，改变了家庭园艺做法。
comments.quote_zh: 这是一个很长的视频，但它彻底改变了我家庭园艺的做法。
comments.text_zh: 这是因为现代耕作方式——重度翻耕、施肥和种植单一作物——消灭了土壤中的生命。失去生命的土壤更容易被侵蚀，而且无论种什么都需要越来越多的合成肥料。美国流失的土壤已经超过其生产出的粮食总量。通过改变耕作方式、培育有生命的土壤，土壤肥力可以恢复到历史水平。把土壤当作活的生命体来对待，好处包括提高肥力、水分入渗、保水性、养分有效性，以及减少或消除对合成肥料的需求。[LINK] 这是一个很长的视频，但它彻底改变了我家庭园艺的做法。[VIDEO]
comments.text: This happened due to extermination of soil life through modern farming practices of heavy tilling, fertilizing and monoculture crops. Dead soil is more susceptible to erosion and requires ever increasing amounts of synthetic fertilizer to grow anything. More soil has been lost from the US than the amount of food that has been produced. Soil fertility can be returned to historical levels by changing farming practices to make living soil. The benefits of treating the soil as a living organism include increased fertility, water infiltration, moisture retention, and nutrient availability as well as decreasing or eliminating synthetic fertilizer requirements. [LINK] This is a long video but it has completely changed my home gardening practices. [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: YouTube 上的土壤健康视频有你需要的一切。Gabe Brown 和 Ray Archuleta 的演讲很容易看进去。Elaine Ingham 博士更关注土壤生命，细节比多数人在意的还多，但她确实提供了一些理解根际相互作用的重要细节。Living Web Farms 有很多关于再生实践的讲座。关于土壤健康的学术论文也多得数不清。Gabe Brown 的这个视频 [VIDEO] 让我走上了再生之路。如果你不想花几个小时看信息，这里就是要点。土壤是活的。植物把微生物和真菌当作外部的胃。直射阳光和扰动/翻耕会杀死土壤生命。土壤里没有生命，最终会变成沙漠，因为有机物被风化从沙子里筛走。
comments.text: YouTube soil health videos has all you need. Gabe Brown and Ray Archuleta presentations are easy to consume. Dr. Elaine Ingham focuses more on the soil life in greater detail than most care about but she does provide some important to understand details on rhizosphere interactions. Living Web Farms has quite a lot of lectures about regenerative practices. There are also a myriad of academic papers on soil health as well. This video, [VIDEO] , by Gabe Brown set me on the regenerative path. If you dont want to consume hours of information here is the gist. The soil is alive. Plants use microbes and fungus as an external stomach. Direct sun and disruption/tilling kill the soil life. Without life in the soil you eventually have a desert as the organics are sifted out of the sand by weathering.

comments.text_zh: Gabe Brown 在这场关于再生农业的讲座中提到了这一点。抱歉，我没有时间戳，我看这个已经过去几周了。[VIDEO] 我不是农业专家，但我确实懂一点植物生物学。我的理解是，他说的是大气中的 CO2 与肥料结合会提高植物的生长速度，但植物并不会按比例吸收更多的其他微量营养素，要么是因为它在生物学上受到速率限制，要么是因为它无法获取。我另外搜了些资料，表明这可能是选择性育种挑出长得更快但营养更少的作物造成的结果，但那似乎会是一个相关的问题。那些作物往往是因为能在合成肥料和 *-cides 下生长而被选中的，缺乏营养价值只是意外后果。
comments.text: Gabe Brown mentioned it in this lecture on regenerative agriculture. Sorry, but I don't have a timestamp, it's been a few weeks since I watched it. [VIDEO] I'm not an expert in farming, but I do know a little bit of plant biology. My understanding of what he said was that the combination of atmospheric CO2 and fertilizer increases the growth rate of the plant, but the plant doesn't uptake a proportionately larger amount of other micro nutrients, either because it is biologically rate limited or doesn't have access. Other Googling suggests that it could be a result of selective breeding picking crops that grow faster but are less nutritious, but that would seem to be a correlated problem. Those crops tend to be selected for their ability to grow with synthetic fertilizer and *-cides, with the lack of nutritional value being an unintended consequence.

comments.story_title: A soil-science revolution upends plans to fight climate change
comments.text_zh: “一茶匙健康土壤中所含的细菌、真菌和其他微生物，比地球上的人还多。这些饥饿的微生物会让土壤很难在长时间内储存碳。”土壤微生物的自然呼吸量，与可持续农业实践下健康土壤能自然固存的碳量相比，是很小的。众所周知，健康土壤能储存大量碳，而这些生物正与之共存。不可持续的农业实践（单一栽培、单季种植、让田地休耕、翻耕、化学喷洒，基本上就是孟山都的整个商业模式）的发展，破坏了土壤的生物多样性和健康。健康土壤每几分钟就能吸收一英寸的降雨。田地会被淹（随后作物损失），是因为地面又硬又结壳，阻碍了土壤吸收。如果更多农田土壤具有像茅屋奶酪那样的健康质地，洪水就不会成为问题。是的，在健康土壤存在的情况下，强制固碳可能行不通。然而，修复全世界因不可持续的工业化农业实践而造成的退化土壤，会自然地固存碳。我很想知道，过去100多年不可持续的工业化农业，究竟让我们土壤中少了多少曾经被固定的碳。[VIDEO] [LINK]
comments.text: "One teaspoon of healthy soil contains more bacteria, fungi and other microbes than there are humans on Earth. Those hungry organisms can make soil a difficult place to store carbon over long periods of time." The natural respiration of soil microbes is small compared to how much carbon can be naturally sequestered in healthy soil due to sustainable agricultural practices. Healthy soil is well-known to hold substantial amounts of carbon, right along side such organisms. The development of unsustainable agricultural practices (monocultures, single-planting seasons, letting fields lie fallow, tilling, chemical sprays, essentially Monsanto's entire business model) has destroyed soil biodiversity and health. Healthy soil can absorb an inch of rain every few minutes. Fields flood (and crops are subsequently lost) because the ground is hard and crusty, preventing soil absorption. If more cropland soil had the healthy consistency of cottage cheese, flooding wouldn't be an issue. Yes, forced carbon sequestration might not work in the presence of healthy soil. However, fixing the deficient soils created across the world from unsustainable industrial agriculture practices will naturally sequester carbon. I would love to know exactly how much carbon no longer is trapped in our soils that once was due to the last 100+ years of unsustainable industrialized agriculture. [VIDEO] [LINK]

comments.author: imtringued
comments.story_title: Mangroves on a Landfill
comments.why_zh: 为再生农业辩护时引用的。
comments.text_zh: 我不知道你看的是什么骗局，但再生农业极其复杂且耗时，不过并不需要大量体力劳动，因为它与机械化兼容。传统农业是简单而懒惰的版本：与其试图理解你当地的生态系统，你只需把所有东西都浇上化肥、农药等等，这样你就不必关心土壤里发生了什么。[VIDEO]
comments.text: I don't know what scams you are looking at but regenerative agriculture is incredibly complicated and time consuming but not physically labor intensive because it is compatible with mechanization. Conventional argiculture is the simple and lazy version where instead of trying to understand your local ecosystem you just douse everything in fertilizer, pesticide, etc so you don't have to care what is happening in your soil. [VIDEO]
